1	# Epic 6 Context: Conversational Memory, Save-to-Journal & Insights
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Users hold a persistent, multi-session conversation with an assistant whose answers are grounded in semantic retrieval over their own past Entries — not generic replies — can turn their own reflective chat messages into real journal Entries with one tap, and occasionally receive an unprompted insight about a pattern in their own writing. None of this (dropped streams, save failures, insight-generation failures) may ever block, corrupt, or freeze the core chat experience. This epic is the product's central differentiator: proving the memory-over-own-history bet end-to-end against the real backend.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 6.1: Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response
12	- Story 6.2: Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation
13	- Story 6.3: Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock
14	- Story 6.4: Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry
15	- Story 6.5: Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation
16	
17	## Requirements & Constraints
18	
19	- Chat responses stream via SSE and must be grounded in retrieval over the user's own Entries; exactly three visible states exist for a response: streaming/processing, error, complete — no others.
20	- A Chat Message never auto-creates an Entry; saving one to the journal (this epic's story 6.4) is the sole explicit exception.
21	- A user holds multiple named Chat Sessions, switchable and startable from the side menu; starting a new session requires connectivity (blocked offline, consistent with the offline composer lock). A returning session restores its last scroll position.
22	- A dropped response stream keeps the partial message on screen with a failure indicator (never clears bubble content) and is recoverable via a dedicated retry call that regenerates without duplicating the original question.
23	- Offline disables the message composer (and the new-session entry point) with an offline banner, while existing history remains fully visible/scrollable.
24	- The save-to-journal (bookmark) affordance appears only on the user's own messages, never on AI responses; it creates an Entry carrying a reference back to the source chat message, through the same shared entries-feature use case introduced earlier in delivery — never by importing the entries repository/data source directly.
25	- Saving the same message twice is idempotent: no duplicate Entry, no conflict surfaced to the user (success, not error).
26	- A save failure never freezes the chat session or the button — the button returns to a retryable state and the rest of the session stays usable.
27	- An Insight is injected into the active session on exactly one trigger per satisfied window — either N user messages sent or a fixed inactivity timeout, whichever comes first — never both, never twice for the same window.
28	- An Insight-generation failure is silent to the user: no error overlay, composer stays enabled, ordinary chat keeps working. Insight quality/content is explicitly outside acceptance scope — only the trigger/injection/failure-isolation mechanism is graded.
29	- Dismissing an Insight never affects scroll position or any other conversation state.
30	
31	## Technical Decisions
32	
33	- Feature lives at `features/chat/`; it consumes `features/entries/`'s abstract save/create-entry port from `entries/domain` only — never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (layering invariant, zero violations tolerated).
34	- Repositories return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`, except the chat response itself, which is `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` given its SSE nature. The closed, 14-member `Failure` hierarchy (13 server codes + a local-only malformed-response code) is shared from `core/` and never redefined per feature.
35	- Chat holds no local write queue: a send attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to a `networkOffline` failure, never queued. Plain history reads (sessions, messages) transparently fall back to the local cache; retry logic for retryable failure codes lives once in the shared API client, not reimplemented per feature.
36	- Chat's message/streaming state is its own sealed state class (append-only, streaming-aware) — explicitly excluded from the shared generic `Resource<T>` single-fetch state pattern, because it isn't a single fetch.
37	- The proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto the existing chat state from story 6.1, never a second parallel state container.
38	- A never-throws `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` helper (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped) ships with this epic's first consumer (the save-to-journal story) and is reused unawaited (fire-and-forget) by the insight story so a slow/failed insight never blocks or delays the chat stream.
39	- No BLoC/Cubit ever takes another BLoC/Cubit as a constructor dependency, in this feature or across features; independent state sources compose via injected domain streams/use-cases or `BlocListener`, never a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
40	- The entries-owning feature's save port is idempotent on the save-to-journal identifier at the implementation level (not just the type signature) — a repeat save for the same source message never creates a second Entry.
41	- Session/message/sync-badge local caching follows the same per-feature local-cache-box convention used by other features; cursor-based pagination for session and message lists follows the server's own cursor convention verbatim.
42	
43	## UX & Interaction Patterns
44	
45	- Chat bubbles: user (sage, squared bottom-right corner) vs. AI (ivory, squared bottom-left, resting elevation). A streaming AI bubble adds a blinking cursor at the text's end and nothing else changes visually while generating; under Reduce Motion the cursor blink is skipped and final text shows immediately instead.
46	- A dropped/failed response replaces the bubble's timestamp slot with red retry copy; bubble text itself is never cleared.
47	- Bookmark button: four states on every user message only — idle (outline) / saving (spinner, or a static label under Reduce Motion) / saved (ochre check) / error (red warning). Tapping an already-saved message is a no-op. State must be carried by icon + color together, never color alone. Tap target ≥44pt.
48	- Insight card: ochre left spine, mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" — the spine is the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream itself.
49	- Offline banner disables sending only; conversation history stays scrollable and readable underneath it. A session-expired overlay (re-auth) can appear over chat without losing scroll position or in-memory history.
50	- A new session opens with the composer focused and only the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no invented greeting copy.
51	- No swipe gestures, no nested overlays, no pull-to-refresh beyond what the session/message endpoints already govern.
52	
53	## Cross-Story Dependencies
54	
55	- Story 6.1 establishes the chat stream/state machine that 6.2 (sessions), 6.3 (retry/offline), 6.4 (bookmark), and 6.5 (insight overlay) all build on or append to.

# Epic 6 Context: Conversational Memory, Save-to-Journal & Insights

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Users hold a persistent, multi-session conversation with an assistant whose answers are grounded in semantic retrieval over their own past Entries — not generic replies — can turn their own reflective chat messages into real journal Entries with one tap, and occasionally receive an unprompted insight about a pattern in their own writing. None of this (dropped streams, save failures, insight-generation failures) may ever block, corrupt, or freeze the core chat experience. This epic is the product's central differentiator: proving the memory-over-own-history bet end-to-end against the real backend.

## Stories

- Story 6.1: Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response
- Story 6.2: Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation
- Story 6.3: Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock
- Story 6.4: Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry
- Story 6.5: Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation

## Requirements & Constraints

- Chat responses stream via SSE and must be grounded in retrieval over the user's own Entries; exactly three visible states exist for a response: streaming/processing, error, complete — no others.
- A Chat Message never auto-creates an Entry; saving one to the journal (this epic's story 6.4) is the sole explicit exception.
- A user holds multiple named Chat Sessions, switchable and startable from the side menu; starting a new session requires connectivity (blocked offline, consistent with the offline composer lock). A returning session restores its last scroll position.
- A dropped response stream keeps the partial message on screen with a failure indicator (never clears bubble content) and is recoverable via a dedicated retry call that regenerates without duplicating the original question.
- Offline disables the message composer (and the new-session entry point) with an offline banner, while existing history remains fully visible/scrollable.
- The save-to-journal (bookmark) affordance appears only on the user's own messages, never on AI responses; it creates an Entry carrying a reference back to the source chat message, through the same shared entries-feature use case introduced earlier in delivery — never by importing the entries repository/data source directly.
- Saving the same message twice is idempotent: no duplicate Entry, no conflict surfaced to the user (success, not error).
- A save failure never freezes the chat session or the button — the button returns to a retryable state and the rest of the session stays usable.
- An Insight is injected into the active session on exactly one trigger per satisfied window — either N user messages sent or a fixed inactivity timeout, whichever comes first — never both, never twice for the same window.
- An Insight-generation failure is silent to the user: no error overlay, composer stays enabled, ordinary chat keeps working. Insight quality/content is explicitly outside acceptance scope — only the trigger/injection/failure-isolation mechanism is graded.
- Dismissing an Insight never affects scroll position or any other conversation state.

## Technical Decisions

- Feature lives at `features/chat/`; it consumes `features/entries/`'s abstract save/create-entry port from `entries/domain` only — never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (layering invariant, zero violations tolerated).
- Repositories return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`, except the chat response itself, which is `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` given its SSE nature. The closed, 14-member `Failure` hierarchy (13 server codes + a local-only malformed-response code) is shared from `core/` and never redefined per feature.
- Chat holds no local write queue: a send attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to a `networkOffline` failure, never queued. Plain history reads (sessions, messages) transparently fall back to the local cache; retry logic for retryable failure codes lives once in the shared API client, not reimplemented per feature.
- Chat's message/streaming state is its own sealed state class (append-only, streaming-aware) — explicitly excluded from the shared generic `Resource<T>` single-fetch state pattern, because it isn't a single fetch.
- The proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto the existing chat state from story 6.1, never a second parallel state container.
- A never-throws `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` helper (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped) ships with this epic's first consumer (the save-to-journal story) and is reused unawaited (fire-and-forget) by the insight story so a slow/failed insight never blocks or delays the chat stream.
- No BLoC/Cubit ever takes another BLoC/Cubit as a constructor dependency, in this feature or across features; independent state sources compose via injected domain streams/use-cases or `BlocListener`, never a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
- The entries-owning feature's save port is idempotent on the save-to-journal identifier at the implementation level (not just the type signature) — a repeat save for the same source message never creates a second Entry.
- Session/message/sync-badge local caching follows the same per-feature local-cache-box convention used by other features; cursor-based pagination for session and message lists follows the server's own cursor convention verbatim.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Chat bubbles: user (sage, squared bottom-right corner) vs. AI (ivory, squared bottom-left, resting elevation). A streaming AI bubble adds a blinking cursor at the text's end and nothing else changes visually while generating; under Reduce Motion the cursor blink is skipped and final text shows immediately instead.
- A dropped/failed response replaces the bubble's timestamp slot with red retry copy; bubble text itself is never cleared.
- Bookmark button: four states on every user message only — idle (outline) / saving (spinner, or a static label under Reduce Motion) / saved (ochre check) / error (red warning). Tapping an already-saved message is a no-op. State must be carried by icon + color together, never color alone. Tap target ≥44pt.
- Insight card: ochre left spine, mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" — the spine is the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream itself.
- Offline banner disables sending only; conversation history stays scrollable and readable underneath it. A session-expired overlay (re-auth) can appear over chat without losing scroll position or in-memory history.
- A new session opens with the composer focused and only the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no invented greeting copy.
- No swipe gestures, no nested overlays, no pull-to-refresh beyond what the session/message endpoints already govern.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 6.1 establishes the chat stream/state machine that 6.2 (sessions), 6.3 (retry/offline), 6.4 (bookmark), and 6.5 (insight overlay) all build on or append to.
- Story 6.4 is this epic's (and the codebase's) first consumer of the shared `isolated_side_effect` helper; Story 6.5 reuses that same helper fire-and-forget.
- Story 6.4 depends on the entries feature's save/create-entry port already existing from earlier delivery work; it must not introduce a second entry model or reach into entries' data layer.
- Story 6.5's insight overlay is layered onto 6.1's chat state rather than a separate state container, so it cannot be built independently of 6.1's state shape.

These are legitimate, well-tested fixes on their own terms (each has a regression test, per `test-summary.md`), and the deferred-work.md/spec-6-2 round-2 entries are internally consistent about this. But it means the handed-off diff does not "represent exactly story 6.3's implementation work" as the audit brief assumed — it's 6.2-round-2 + 6.3 bundled together. Worth confirming with whoever is tracking per-story diffs that this bundling was intentional (e.g., both were uncommitted in the same working tree when 6.3 started).

The team's own self-review in this diff (deferred-work.md, spec Review Findings sections) is thorough and already catches several real issues; the findings below are either genuinely new (not in that self-review) or worth reconsidering even though the author chose to defer them.
  
  - `ConnectivityPlusWatcher` (and `connectivity_plus` generally) only reports whether a network *interface* is up, not whether the device actually has working internet — a device joined to a dead Wi-Fi/captive portal, or a Wi-Fi with no WAN, is reported "online." The offline banner and composer lock never engage in that case even though `sendMessage`/`retryMessage` will still fail. Neither the spec's Design Notes nor the Code Map acknowledge this gap between interface-connectivity and real reachability, and nothing reconciles `ChatReady.isOffline` with the repository's own independent `Failure.networkOffline` detection — the two "offline" signals can disagree on screen at the same time (composer enabled by `ConnectivityWatcher` while a send simultaneously fails as `NetworkOffline`), and Boundaries explicitly forbids touching the latter to fix it.
  
  - The new `_OfflineBanner` (`lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`) has no `Semantics`/live-region treatment announcing its appearance or disappearance to a screen-reader user. The exact same a11y gap is already called out for session switches in `deferred-work.md` (story 6.2), but it wasn't captured as a deferred item for this new banner.
  
  - `test/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble_test.dart`'s new Semantics test only proves `Semantics(button: true)` is present when `onRetry` is supplied. No test proves the opposite — that a `failed` bubble built with `onRetry: null` does *not* expose a button semantics node — even though the production code comment explicitly calls that out as something that "must never" happen.
  
  - No test exercises `ChatCubit.close()` while a `retryMessage()` call is in flight. The "cancel() alone leaves the returned Future permanently unresolved" bug (documented in `chat_cubit.dart`'s updated comment) is now fixed generically via the shared `_consumeStream`, but the regression test for it was never duplicated/extended from `sendMessage` to `retryMessage` to prove the fix actually covers the new call path too.
  
  - `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` documents `chat-messages-retry`'s own SSE order as `message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error` — identical to `sendMessage`. Every new retry test (`chat_remote_data_source_test.dart`, `chat_cubit_test.dart`) only drives `message_created`/`token`/`done`/error; the `context` event's behavior through the shared helper is never exercised for this new endpoint at all.
  
  - `pubspec.lock` newly pulls in `dbus`, `nm`, `xml`, and `petitparser` — `connectivity_plus`'s Linux-only transitive dependencies — into a project that has no `android/` directory and only ships `ios/`. These packages can never run on the target platform; worth at least a comment noting the trade-off was accepted knowingly.
  
  - The no-`serverId` retry fallback silently resends the user's original content via a brand-new `chat-messages-send` call. If message creation has any server-side side effects (RAG indexing, `userMessageCount`, insight-trigger counters tied to message count), a "retry" after an early drop could create two persisted copies of logically the same question server-side. Nothing in the spec or tests addresses whether that server-side duplication is actually safe — only the client-side "one bubble" view is verified.
  
  - `ChatRepositoryImpl.retryMessage` is documented/tested as a "pure passthrough, no Hive persistence" — same as `sendMessage`. But a successful retry replaces the *content* of an already-cached message id without ever writing the new content back to the offline cache; if the app is force-closed right after a successful retry and relaunched offline, the cached copy of that message would still show stale/failed content. Not called out anywhere as a known limitation.
  
  - Both new un-`buildWhen`-guarded `BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>`s (`AppDrawer`'s "Novo Chat" disable, the offline banner) are deferred in `deferred-work.md` as low-cost debt — but a trivial `buildWhen` (e.g. `(p, c) => p is ChatReady && c is ChatReady && p.isOffline != c.isOffline`) would have been cheap enough to fix inline, unlike the three other round-2 findings in this same diff that *were* promoted from "defer" to "patch" and fixed outright. Worth reconsidering why this one wasn't.
  
  - The offline I/O matrix only covers clean "goes offline" / "comes back online" transitions. There's no test for a flapping connection (rapid true/false/true emissions, or a transition arriving mid-stream while a send/retry is actively running) verifying the banner/composer don't visibly flicker or leave `_isSending` state inconsistent.
  
  - `ConnectivityWatcher.watch()`'s own interface doc (`lib/features/chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart`) makes no statement about single-vs-multiple-call expectations. `ConnectivityPlusWatcher.watch()`'s implementation builds a brand-new, single-subscription `StreamController` and a brand-new live `onConnectivityChanged` subscription on every call — safe today because only `ChatCubit`'s constructor ever calls it once, but nothing documents that as a constraint, so a future second caller resolving the same DI singleton and calling `.watch()` again would silently get an independent duplicate platform-channel listener rather than sharing one.
  
  - The spec's Boundaries say retry "reuses `_isSending` verbatim" and is a no-op while one is in flight, but there's no widget-level (as opposed to cubit-level) test proving a rapid double-tap on the retry copy in `chat_bubble_test.dart`/`chat_screen_test.dart` is actually swallowed by the UI — only the cubit unit test covers the "second retry while one is in flight" case.
  
  Files most relevant to these findings: `lib/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart`, `lib/features/chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart`, `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart`, `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`, `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart`, `lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart`, `test/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble_test.dart`, `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart`, `test/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source_test.dart`, `pubspec.lock`, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` (read-only reference, confirms the `context` SSE event in the contract).
</agent-message>

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

- [ ] [Review][Patch] Add an e2e regression test for the stale-`_sendSubscription`-nulling fix — a second `sendMessage`/`retryMessage` on the same cubit after a prior one completed could hang again if this regresses, and no current test (fake-stream-backed) would catch it [lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:479]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Add a regression test for `ChatCubit.close()` while `retryMessage()` is in-flight — the "cancel() alone leaves the Future unresolved" bug's existing regression test covers `sendMessage` but was never duplicated for `retryMessage` [lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:432]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Wrap `ConnectivityPlusWatcher.watch()`'s `onConnectivityChanged.listen()` call in try/catch, mirroring the already-guarded `checkConnectivity()` seed path right beside it [lib/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart:40]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Add a negative-case test proving a `failed` bubble built with `onRetry: null` exposes no button semantics node, matching the code's own "must never" comment [lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart:136]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Add retry-path test coverage for the `context` SSE event — `openapi.yaml` documents the same event order for `chat-messages-retry` as `sendMessage`, but no retry test exercises it [lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Document `ConnectivityWatcher.watch()`'s single-vs-multiple-call contract — safe today with one caller, but undocumented as a constraint [lib/features/chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] Add a widget-level test proving a rapid double-tap on the retry affordance is swallowed — only the cubit-level "second retry while in flight" case is covered today [lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart]
- [x] [Review][Defer] `ConnectivityPlusWatcher` reports interface state, not real reachability — the composer can show enabled while a send simultaneously fails as `NetworkOffline`; mitigated in practice by this same story's own tap-to-retry affordance, and reconciling the two signals would mean touching `ChatRepositoryImpl`'s existing `networkOffline` handling, which this story's Boundaries forbid [lib/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart] — deferred, pre-existing architectural trade-off
- [x] [Review][Defer] No test covers a flapping connectivity signal (rapid on/off/on, or a transition arriving mid-send) verifying the banner/composer/`_isSending` stay consistent — expected behavior for this case is unspecified anywhere in the spec [lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] `ChatRepositoryImpl.retryMessage` never writes a successful retry's new content back to the Hive cache — stale cached content could reappear after an offline relaunch right after a successful retry; mirrors `sendMessage`'s existing no-persist-on-success design from story 6.1, not newly introduced here [lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart:125] — deferred, pre-existing

2	
3	import '../../../../core/design_tokens.dart';
4	import '../../domain/entities/chat_message.dart';
5	import '../cubit/chat_state.dart';
6	
7	/// Review finding: shared by the `Semantics.label` and the visible `Text`
8	/// below so a future copy edit can't desync the spoken label from what's
9	/// actually on screen.
10	const _retryCopy = 'Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente';
11	
12	/// One message bubble — user (Boundaries: `colorChatBubbleUser`, squared
13	/// bottom-right corner) vs AI (`colorSurfaceElevated`, squared bottom-left
14	/// corner, resting [DesignTokens.elevation1]). Exactly the 3 visible
15	/// states RF04's Acceptance Criteria names render here, driven by
16	/// [ChatUiMessage.status]: `streaming` (progressive text + blinking
17	/// cursor), `failed` (spec-6-3: a tappable tap-to-retry indicator replaces
18	/// the timestamp slot, invoking [onRetry]), `complete` (plain text,
19	/// nothing else). [ChatUiMessage.content] itself is rendered as-is in
20	/// every state — never cleared on failure (I/O matrix).
21	class ChatBubble extends StatefulWidget {
22	  const ChatBubble({required this.message, this.onRetry, super.key});
23	
24	  final ChatUiMessage message;
25	
26	  /// spec-6-3 — invoked when the user taps a `failed` AI bubble's own
27	  /// retry copy; `null` on a user bubble (never shown there, only an AI
28	  /// response ever fails) or whenever a caller has nothing to wire it to.
29	  final VoidCallback? onRetry;
30	
31	  @override
32	  State<ChatBubble> createState() => _ChatBubbleState();
33	}
34	
35	class _ChatBubbleState extends State<ChatBubble>
36	    with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
37	  late final AnimationController _cursorController;
38	
39	  @override
40	  void initState() {
41	    super.initState();
42	    _cursorController = AnimationController(
43	      vsync: this,
44	      duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 600),
45	    );
46	    _syncCursorAnimation();
47	  }
48	
49	  @override
50	  void didUpdateWidget(ChatBubble oldWidget) {
51	    super.didUpdateWidget(oldWidget);
52	    _syncCursorAnimation();
53	  }
54	
55	  /// Keeps the ticker running only while actually needed — a message
56	  /// that finalizes to `complete`/`failed` must stop ticking forever
57	  /// after, both so a long-lived chat session never leaks one live
58	  /// `AnimationController` per past message, and so nothing waiting on
59	  /// "every animation in the tree has settled" (e.g. a test's own
60	  /// `pumpAndSettle()`) ever blocks on a bubble that finished streaming.
61	  void _syncCursorAnimation() {
62	    final shouldAnimate = widget.message.status == ChatMessageStatus.streaming;
63	    if (shouldAnimate && !_cursorController.isAnimating) {
64	      _cursorController.repeat(reverse: true);
65	    } else if (!shouldAnimate && _cursorController.isAnimating) {
66	      _cursorController.stop();
67	    }
68	  }
69	
70	  @override
71	  void dispose() {
72	    _cursorController.dispose();
73	    super.dispose();
74	  }
75	
76	  @override
77	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
78	    final message = widget.message;
79	    final onRetry = widget.onRetry;
80	    final isUser = message.role == ChatMessageRole.user;
81	    // Boundaries: "cursor skipped under
82	    // `MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations`" — the real token text
83	    // itself always reveals as real tokens actually arrive (there is no
84	    // separate typing-speed animation to collapse here), only the
85	    // blinking-cursor glyph is conditional on Reduce Motion.
86	    final reduceMotion = MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations;
87	    final showCursor =
88	        message.status == ChatMessageStatus.streaming && !reduceMotion;
89	
90	    // spec-6-3 Boundaries: tap-to-retry copy, tappable, 44pt min tap
91	    // target — replaces the earlier generic (non-tappable) error
92	    // indicator. The visible copy renders identically either way;
93	    // `Semantics(button: true)` only wraps it when [onRetry] is actually
94	    // supplied (review finding) — a bubble built with no retry callback
95	    // must never be announced to a screen reader as a working button.
96	    final retryIndicator = InkWell(
97	      onTap: onRetry,
98	      borderRadius: const BorderRadius.all(
99	        Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm),
100	      ),
101	      child: ConstrainedBox(
102	        constraints: const BoxConstraints(
103	          minHeight: DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin,
104	        ),
105	        child: Container(
106	          alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
107	          padding: DesignTokens.chatFailureIndicatorPadding,
108	          decoration: const BoxDecoration(
109	            color: DesignTokens.colorErrorBg,
110	            borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(
111	              Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm),
112	            ),
113	          ),
114	          child: Text(
115	            _retryCopy,
116	            style: DesignTokens.textCaptionSm.copyWith(
117	              color: DesignTokens.colorError,
118	            ),
119	          ),
120	        ),
121	      ),
122	    );
123	    final retryIndicatorWithSemantics = onRetry == null
124	        ? retryIndicator
125	        : Semantics(
126	            button: true,
127	            label: _retryCopy,
128	            excludeSemantics: true,
129	            child: retryIndicator,
130	          );
131	
132	    return Align(
133	      alignment: isUser ? Alignment.centerRight : Alignment.centerLeft,
134	      child: Container(
135	        margin: const EdgeInsets.only(bottom: DesignTokens.chatBubbleGap),
136	        constraints: BoxConstraints(
137	          maxWidth:
138	              MediaQuery.of(context).size.width *
139	              DesignTokens.chatBubbleMaxWidthFraction,
140	        ),
141	        padding: DesignTokens.chatBubblePadding,
142	        decoration: BoxDecoration(
143	          color: isUser
144	              ? DesignTokens.colorChatBubbleUser
145	              : DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated,
146	          borderRadius: BorderRadius.only(
147	            topLeft: const Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusMd),
148	            topRight: const Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusMd),
149	            bottomLeft: Radius.circular(isUser ? DesignTokens.radiusMd : 0),
150	            bottomRight: Radius.circular(isUser ? 0 : DesignTokens.radiusMd),
151	          ),
152	          boxShadow: isUser ? null : DesignTokens.elevation1,
153	        ),
154	        child: Column(
155	          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
156	          mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
157	          children: [
158	            Text.rich(
159	              TextSpan(
160	                children: [
161	                  TextSpan(text: message.content),
162	                  if (showCursor)
163	                    WidgetSpan(
164	                      alignment: PlaceholderAlignment.middle,
165	                      child: ExcludeSemantics(
166	                        child: FadeTransition(
167	                          opacity: _cursorController,
168	                          child: const Text('▏'),
169	                        ),
170	                      ),
171	                    ),
172	                ],
173	              ),
174	              style: DesignTokens.textBodyLg.copyWith(
175	                color: DesignTokens.colorTextPrimary,
176	              ),
177	            ),
178	            if (message.status == ChatMessageStatus.failed) ...[
179	              const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingXs),
180	              retryIndicatorWithSemantics,
181	            ],
182	          ],
183	        ),
184	      ),
185	    );
186	  }
187	}

All 967 tests passed, `flutter analyze` reports zero issues. All 7 patches applied and verified.

## ✅ Code review actions complete

- Decision-needed resolved: 0
- Patches handled: 7 (all applied and verified — `fvm flutter analyze`: 0 issues, `fvm flutter test`: 967/967 passing)
- Deferred: 3
- Dismissed: 6

**What was fixed:**
1. Added an e2e regression test (`chat_flow_e2e_test.dart`) proving a second `sendMessage()` on the same cubit after a prior one completed resolves promptly through the *real* Dio subscription — closing the gap where the fake-`StreamController`-backed unit tests couldn't catch a regression of the stale-subscription-nulling fix.
2. Added a `close()`-while-`retryMessage()`-in-flight regression test (`chat_cubit_test.dart`), extending the same coverage class to the new retry path.
3. Wrapped `ConnectivityPlusWatcher.watch()`'s `onConnectivityChanged.listen()` call in try/catch, mirroring the already-guarded `checkConnectivity()` seed path, plus a test proving a synchronous throw there no longer escapes `watch()`.
4. Added a negative-case test proving a `failed` bubble with `onRetry: null` exposes no button semantics node.
5. Added retry-path test coverage for the `context` SSE event.
6. Documented `ConnectivityWatcher.watch()`'s single-vs-multiple-call contract.
7. Added a widget-level test proving a rapid double-tap on the retry affordance only fires one `chat-messages-retry` call.

Since all `patch`/`decision-needed` items are resolved and only acknowledged, pre-existing trade-offs remain deferred, story 6-3's status moves to `done`.
